title: Applied ML Evals: Eval Harness & Regression Playbook (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Applied ML best practices for Redwood Inference evals: the eval harness, prompt-set and benchmark management, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profiling, and the regression triage workflow. It is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML, and SREs responsible for model quality and rollout decisions.

Goals:
- Provide a reproducible eval harness and CI integration for automated quality checks.
- Maintain a curated prompt-sets and benchmark registry that captures business-critical behaviors.
- Standardize model onboarding criteria (performance, cost, safety).
- Define quantization profiles and expected performance/cost tradeoffs.
- Define a clear regression triage and rollback playbook with owners and SLAs.

Ownership & Contacts:
- Document owner: Applied ML (engineering)
- Primary contact: Aisha Patel (aisha.patel@redwood.example.com)
- On-call triage: Applied ML rotation (see /eng-oncall schedule)

1) Eval Harness (architecture & CI integration)
- Summary: The eval harness runs unit and scenario-level tests against candidate model artifacts. It supports multiple test types: functional (task correctness), distributional (statistical metrics over a prompt set), safety (policy/L0 checks), and latency/cost profiling.
- Components:
  - runner: Python CLI (rwi-eval-runner) that loads a model artifact, runs prompt sets, and writes standardized JSON results to S3 (/evals/results/YYYYMMDD/).
  - schema: all results follow the eval-result schema (fields: run_id, model_version, dataset_id, metric, value, unit, seed, tags).
  - CI: GitHub Actions + internal buildkite pipeline that gates pull requests touching models, prompt sets, or eval logic.
- How to run locally:
  1. Checkout repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood/eval-harness.git
  2. Activate venv: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
  3. Install: pip install -e .[dev]
  4. Run example: rwi-eval-runner --model artifacts/models/xgpt-v1/ --prompts prompts/qa/crypto-10k.jsonl --out results/xgpt-v1-crypto.json
- CI gating rules:
  - Must run full-unit and smoke suite for PRs changing model scoring logic.
  - Any PR that changes a prompt set or introduces a new metric requires at least two approvers (Applied ML + Product).

2) Prompt Sets & Benchmarks
- Registry structure (on S3 /evals/prompt-sets and mirrored in the confluence index): each prompt-set is a JSONL with metadata header containing: id, owner, intent(tags), dataset_size, language, created_at, review_cycle_days, and acceptance_criteria.
- Metadata example:
  {
    "id": "qa-crypto-2025",
    "owner": "applied-ml",
    "intent": ["FAQ", "financial"],
    "dataset_size": "10000",
    "language": "en",
    "created_at": "2025-03-12",
    "review_cycle_days": "90"
  }
- Benchmark metrics we track (per prompt-set):
  - accuracy / exact-match (task-dependent)
  - BLEU / ROUGE / F1 (generation tasks)
  - MRR / NDCG (ranking tasks)
  - perplexity (language-model fit)
  - safety false-positive / false-negative rates
  - latency p50/p90/p99 and tokens/sec cost-per-token
- Benchmark result table (example):
  | metric | target | failure-trigger |
  |--------|--------|-----------------|
  | exact_match | >= 78% | < 76% (block rollout) |
  | perplexity | <= 22 | > 25 (investigate) |
  | safety_fp_rate | <= 0.5% | > 1.0% (P0) |
  | latency_p90 | <= 300ms | > 450ms (degrade) |

3) Model Onboarding Guide (checklist)
- Purpose: a canonical checklist to validate models for production serving on Redwood (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Onboarding steps (must be completed and documented in model registry):
  1. Artifact & provenance: model archive, weights checksum, training data provenance summary, license review.
  2. Functional QA: run full eval harness across canonical prompt sets. Document metrics and pass/fail against acceptance_criteria.
  3. Safety review: run safety suite and manual small-sample review from Product/Safety.
  4. Performance profiling: measure latency (p50/p90/p99) at representative batch sizes and sequence lengths; measure memory and peak GPU util.
  5. Cost estimate: tokens/sec, ops/sec, expected cost-per-1M-tokens under current serving profile.
  6. Quantization compatibility: test with standard quant profiles (see section 5).
  7. Canary plan & rollback criteria: define canary % (recommended 5-10%), monitoring dashboards, regression thresholds, and rollback steps.
- Minimum acceptance criteria (example):
  - Task accuracy >= owner-defined target (documented in prompt-set metadata).
  - Safety FP <= 0.5% and no policy-violating outputs on safety holdout.
  - Latency p90 < 400ms for default 1k-token workload for hosted tier.
  - Cost improvement or parity vs baseline model for the same quality tier when quantized.

4) Quality Guardrails & Monitoring
- Key signals (automated):
  - Quality deltas: absolute metric change vs baseline at 95% CI. Alert if accuracy drops > 2.0 absolute points or perplexity increases > 10%.
  - Safety incidents: any policy-violating output flagged by safety classifier triggers immediate P0 alert.
  - Drift detection: prompt distribution or tokenization OOV rates change > 5%.
  - Latency/CQ: p99 latency increases > 25% or error-rate > 0.5%.
- Alerting and runbooks:
  - Severity mapping: P0 (safety or major user impact), P1 (quality regression above threshold), P2 (performance degradation), P3 (info).
  - Triage SLA: P0 immediate page + 15-minute ack; P1 page + 60-minute ack.
- Auto-rollback policy (applied per-route):
  - If production-run aggregated metric (sliding 1-hour window) exceeds rollback threshold (e.g., accuracy drop > 3% absolute or safety FP > 1%): trigger rollback to previous stable variant and notify owners.

5) Quantization Profiles & Expected Tradeoffs
- Profile registry (canonical names):
  - fp16 (baseline): highest quality, highest memory footprint.
  - int8-static: 2-3x memory reduction, typical quality delta <= 1-2% absolute on classification tasks; large model-specific variance on generation tasks.
  - nf4 / nf4-int8: moderate size reduction with tuned scaling; good quality/cost tradeoff for many transformer decoders.
- Example quantization table:
  | profile | memory delta | expected quality delta | recommended use |
  |--------|--------------|-----------------------|------------------|
  | fp16 | 0% | 0.0 | baseline / safety-critical |
  | int8-static | -60% | -0.5 to -3.0 | cost-sensitive, non-critical generation |
  | nf4 | -45% | -0.3 to -1.5 | general-purpose production |
- Quantization test commands (example):
  rwi-quantize --input artifacts/models/xgpt-v1/model.bin --profile int8-static --out artifacts/models/xgpt-v1-int8/
  rwi-eval-runner --model artifacts/models/xgpt-v1-int8/ --prompts prompts/bench/qa-crypto-2025.jsonl --out results/xgpt-v1-int8-eval.json
- Recommended validation: run full eval harness and manual spot-checking for any generation-based prompt sets. Document observed deltas in model registry entry.

6) Regression Triage Playbook (step-by-step)
- Trigger conditions: failing benchmark thresholds, production alerts, or user-reported quality regressions.
- Triage steps (ordered):
  1. Acknowledge: pager on-call (Applied ML) must acknowledge within SLA.
  2. Collect evidence: latest eval results (CI), production sample traces (IDs, prompts), and diff vs last good run.
  3. Classify regression: functional (metric drop), safety, performance, or infra-related.
  4. Immediate mitigations: if safety or major user impact, rollback to previous variant and set route to read-only.
  5. Root cause analysis: check model artifact (weights checksum), quantization differences, tokenization changes, prompt-set edits, or infra changes (runtime kernels).
  6. Fix & validate: reproduce locally, run targeted evals, staged canary deployment for the fix.
  7. Postmortem: publish within 72 hours for P0/P1 incidents with RCA, timeline, and corrective actions.
- Communication matrix:
  - P0: page execs + customer success (if customer impact) + slack #prod-alerts + incident postmortem.
  - P1: slack #prod-alerts + weekly incident digest.

Appendix: Example eval-run config (json)
{
  "run_id": "run-20260210-001",
  "model_version": "xgpt-v1-int8",
  "dataset_id": "qa-crypto-2025",
  "metrics": ["exact_match", "perplexity", "safety_fp_rate"],
  "batch_size": "8",
  "sequence_length": "1024",
  "seed": "42"
}

Example quick checklist for a new model pull request:
1. Eval harness green for all canonical prompt-sets.
2. Safety suite green and manual spot check completed.
3. Performance profile attached (latency p50/p90/p99).
4. Quantization profiles tested (at least fp16 and nf4).
5. Canary rollout plan and rollback thresholds documented.

Related links and references:
- Eval harness repo: git@github.com:redwood/eval-harness.git
- Model registry: internal dashboard /models
- Monitoring dashboards: /grafana/d/redwood-evals

Review cadence:
- Prompt-sets: review every 90 days or on product change.
- Quantization profiles: review after any major model architecture change or after observed >1% quality delta.
- This playbook: review yearly or after any P0/P1 regression.

Contact the Applied ML team with questions or to request new prompt-sets, benchmark additions, or to schedule a model onboarding review.
